clue.text: Capital author

definitions.meaning: the capital city of the United Kingdom
Jack ..., the American writer of The Call of the Wild

explanation.walkthrough: One of a run of clues in this puzzle pairing a plain word with 'author'.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital city and a writer's surname share the one name here: the English capital and the novelist Jack.

clue.text: Not to be placed where glasses rest

definitions.meaning: in horse-race betting, a stake to win only, rather than each way to finish placed
spectacles sit on the bridge of the face's central feature

explanation.walkthrough: A placed horse finishes second or third; a win-only bet pays nothing for that.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager to win alone is said to be put this way, and the phrase also says where spectacles sit.

clue.text: Conscript tied logs together forming river dam?

indicators.note: a dam sits across a river, so the logs go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
a raft is made of logs lashed together

explanation.surface: A recruit lashes timbers into a barrier across a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming' is a link; the question mark admits that 'dam' is a loose container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is someone drafted into military service, a conscript in American usage.

clue.text: OK without daughter

parts.note: no means lacking, as in 'no money'

explanation.surface: Giving approval, despite having no daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the nod is to signal approval, so the word means assent or the go-ahead.

clue.text: One needing exercise joining sailors in dance — this?

definitions.text: One needing exercise joining sailors in dance — this?

indicators.note: in tells us the sailors go inside the word for dance

parts.note: to hop is to dance or skip
RN is the Royal Navy, crossword shorthand for sailors
one is the Roman numeral I
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A question about which sea dance would suit someone short of exercise, among sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay builds the answer, and the full sentence describes it, a lively dance traditionally done by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional solo dance associated with sailors at sea is exactly what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Weak official author

definitions.meaning: in sport, a referee who favours the home side is called a ...
the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey

explanation.definitionFit: Sports slang names a referee biased to the home team this way, and it is also the Greek epic poet.

clue.text: Similar image became distorted with lens beneath river

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath puts the rearranged letters below the river letter
distorted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lens has warped a picture of a river into something only roughly alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges BECAME and LENS into ESEMBLANCE, set under R by 'beneath'.
explanation.definitionFit: A resemblance is a likeness, something that looks similar to another, which an image can be.

clue.text: Time one put on superb coat

indicators.note: put on places the time word after the word for superb, added to its end

parts.note: plum means excellent, as in a plum job
an age is one long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone takes a while putting on a magnificent coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time one' is taken together as AGE, a single span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's plumage is its covering of feathers, its coat in a loose sense.

clue.text: Author's pen

explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an enclosure for stray animals, a pen, and Ezra the poet carries the same surname.

clue.text: Invest currency in scrap, willynilly

indicators.note: Invest ... in asks for the currency to be put inside the word for scrap

parts.note: an atom is a tiny scrap, as in 'not an atom of truth'
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Advice to put money into scrap metal without any plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'willy-nilly' broken across a line. 'Invest' is the container signal here, as money is put into a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy-nilly means haphazardly, without plan or choice, which is the sense of the two-word phrase.

clue.text: Add oomph to course at university

parts.note: soup is a course of a meal
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Livening up one's studies at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an engine or anything else more power and vigour is an idiom for boosting it.

clue.text: Instrument with a whistle?

parts.note: a playful picture of a percussion instrument whose name begins with a kitchen pot that whistles when it boils

explanation.definitionFit: This is the orchestral timpani, a large drum whose bowl shape resembles a cauldron for boiling water.

clue.text: Girl trailing in group describes Wonka's gobstoppers

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: in puts the trailing word inside the word for group

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of spies or dealers
last means coming at the back, trailing

explanation.surface: A girl lagging behind in a gang is talking about sweets from a famous chocolate factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy Wonka, in Roald Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, invents a sweet that never wears down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahl's confectioner made a gobstopper that never got smaller however long it was sucked, lasting forever.

clue.text: A betrothed princess ——- she dies entombed

parts.note: Princess Ida, of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera, was betrothed in infancy to Prince Hilarion

explanation.surface: An engaged royal heroine meets a grim end, sealed in a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Verdi's Ethiopian princess, who is buried alive with Radames at the end of his opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera heroine ends the work sealed alive in a vault with her lover, dying there.

clue.text: Extra author

definitions.meaning: extra means additional, a further amount

explanation.definitionFit: Additional amounts are 'more', and the Tudor statesman who wrote Utopia carries that surname.

clue.text: Appalling gulf in security as leader's lost in glow of radiation

indicators.note: in places the shaken-up gulf inside the security word
the word for security loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: defence is protection, security

indicators.note: appalling suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful gap in safety measures shows up in a glowing radiation reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'security' is no abstract idea here but a synonym whose first letter is dropped; 'glow of radiation' is the definition, not part of the surface's safety story.
explanation.definitionFit: Effulgence is brilliant radiance, a shining forth of light, so a glow given off fits it.

clue.text: Tailless fish raised back

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, backwards
tailless means the fish name loses its last letter

parts.note: the orfe is a freshwater fish, the ide

explanation.surface: A fish without a tail is lifted out and put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' leaves ORF from ORFE; 'raised' turns it to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'to and fro', the word means back, away from the original direction.

clue.text: Afraid of someone shooting?

parts.note: a person who shies away from a photographer, shooting meaning taking pictures rather than firing a gun

explanation.definitionFit: Someone camera-shy dislikes being photographed, and a photographer is said to shoot pictures.

clue.text: Grammatical term revised, burn a novel

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry writer, having revised, sets fire to the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the ten letters of BURN A NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians use this label for a noun formed from a verb, such as a gerund, so it is a technical term.

clue.text: A sticky thing, it's stuck on old dish from Mexico

parts.note: a burr is a prickly seed head that clings to clothes

explanation.surface: A clinging burr gets stuck on an old Mexican meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stuck on' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of a flour tortilla wrapped round a filling.

clue.text: Meaty author?

definitions.meaning: the meat of a young sheep
Charles ..., the essayist who wrote as Elia

explanation.walkthrough: 'Meaty' is loose for a noun: it hints at the meat itself, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The flesh of a young sheep is a meat, and the Romantic essayist Charles shares that surname.

clue.text: Politician given time to put through new bill

indicators.note: put through means the time word is pushed into the middle of the shuffled bill
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A politician needs time to get a fresh bill through parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Politician' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the definition; 'given' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal is a member of a Liberal party, a politician of that persuasion.

clue.text: Leader essential to Soviets, arguably

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim about which ruler mattered most to the Soviet state.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward Stalin or Lenin; the ruler sits inside 'sovieTS ARguably'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor was the supreme ruler of his country, so a leader in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Racy author

explanation.definitionFit: Racy can mean speedy, and a speedy thing is quick; Jonathan of Gulliver's Travels shares that surname.

clue.text: Composer -—- one shaped by school pupil of his

indicators.note: shaped says the letters of one are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: Alban Berg studied composition under the composer being clued

explanation.surface: A composer is moulded by an academy and taught a student of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped' rearranges ONE to OEN; the composer clued is Arnold Schoenberg, teacher of Alban Berg.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Schoenberg was the Austrian composer who pioneered the twelve-tone method of music.

clue.text: Tough author

definitions.meaning: tough means robust and able to endure
Thomas ... wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.definitionFit: Hardy means robust and able to endure, and Thomas the Wessex novelist carries the name.

clue.text: After goin' on two wheels, one gear in two pieces

indicators.note: after places the I at the end, following the cycling word

parts.note: riding a bicycle is biking; the clipped 'goin'' tells us to drop the final G the same way
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Once you've been out cycling, you change into some two-piece clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is women's swimwear made of two separate parts, top and bottom, so a two-piece outfit.

clue.text: Pass by communist organisation offering aid

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
to cross is to pass over or through

explanation.surface: A communist group drops by with offers of help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just sets CROSS beside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international humanitarian movement providing medical and emergency relief.

clue.text: Haul up rotten fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, hauling up means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: bad means rotten, gone off

explanation.surface: Pulling up a fish that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: The dab is a small flatfish found in European waters.

clue.text: Try long novel on Origin of Species, though hard

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of the word species
novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

explanation.surface: A reader attempts the long book On the Origin of Species, though it is heavy going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the Origin of Species' is Darwin's book, but 'novel' is the anagram signal and 'on' just joins the pieces; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To work hard and to work vigorously are interchangeable adverbs, both meaning with great force.

clue.text: Hard like this to combine tin and oxygen

parts.note: a billy or billycan is a tin cooking pot used by campers
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Mixing tin with oxygen takes a lot of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the idiom 'like billy-o', meaning very hard or vigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'like billy-o' means with great force or energy, so hard is what the phrase intensifies.
